intro: Small configuration formats need an explicit grammar even when they look simple. Splitting only the first equals sign permits values such as tokens or expressions containing equals signs.
task: Parse nonblank key=value lines, splitting only the first separator and rejecting duplicate keys.
requirements: Process nonblank lines after stripping outer whitespace. Split the first = only, trim key and value, and return a dictionary. Keys must be nonempty and unique. Values may be empty or contain more = characters; comments have no special syntax.
Text inputs contain valid Unicode scalar characters and at most 10000 characters. Identifier and dictionary keys are nonempty strings of at most 100 characters.
Return the documented Python output types and preserve all caller inputs. Raise ValueError for invalid inputs unless the task explicitly reports a record-level rejection.

hints.title: Trace one record
hints.body: Use split with a maximum of one split so values retain extra separators.

hints.title: Handle the boundary
hints.body: Check key presence before assignment to avoid silently replacing earlier settings.

explanation: Small configuration formats need an explicit grammar even when they look simple. Splitting only the first equals sign permits values such as tokens or expressions containing equals signs.
Rejecting duplicate keys makes ambiguity visible. A parser that silently keeps the final value can hide a copied setting or a configuration mistake.
